_meta: A set of hue angles in degrees and a rotation amount, used to show why rotating a hue must use circular (wraparound, modulo 360) arithmetic rather than clamping the result to the valid range, because hue is an angle on a color wheel where 360 degrees is the same as 0, so a rotation that pushes a hue past 360 must wrap back around into the reds -- clamping it to the top of the range instead produces the wrong color and collapses distinct hues into the same value. Hue is the angular coordinate of color: 0 is red, 120 is green, 240 is blue, and 360 wraps back to red. It is periodic, so arithmetic on it is arithmetic on a circle. Rotating every hue by some amount (to shift a palette warmer or cooler) means adding the rotation and taking the result modulo 360, so a hue of 340 rotated by 40 becomes 20 (a warm red-orange), having crossed the 360/0 seam. The naive mistake is to treat hue like an ordinary bounded quantity and clamp the sum to the maximum: then 340 + 40 = 380 is clamped to 360 (or 359), a deep magenta-red, which is not where a 40-degree rotation should land it; worse, 340 and 350 both clamp to the same ceiling, collapsing two distinct hues into one, while wrapping sends them to 20 and 30, still distinct. hues is the list of input hue angles; rotation is the amount to add; hue_max is the modulus (360). These are the fixture; the wrapped and the clamped result for each hue, and which hues cross the seam and collide, are computed.
